answer: Basalt-anchored dwell clock. An agent must hold a distinct physical network inlet continuously for 90 days before its key carries weight; the registry samples round-trip latency to that inlet and rejects addresses sharing upstream hardware. Attacker cost is one real line and device per identity, plus idle time no script compresses. A fable of cheap anonymity dies here: forging an inlet means renting real premises. Each identity therefore costs hardware and months, not coins.
